We applied template 20810 to target. It returned a tuple of product precursors? The result shows a tuple of two SMILES: 'CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N1CCN(c2cc(N)cc3c2OC2(CCC2)CC3)CC1' and 'O=S(=O)(Cl)c1ccccc1F'. So the retrosynthetic step splits target into these two precursors.

We need to construct route with at least 6 reactions using templates in order: ['20810', '2895', '1914397', '1914398', '1914399', '74054'].

Thus we need to apply each template sequentially to appropriate molecules, building a tree. Starting from target, apply 20810 gives two precursors. Then we need to apply 2895 to one of those (or both) to further break down, then 1914397, etc. Need at least 6 reactions total, we have 6 templates, each used once in order. So each reaction node corresponds to applying a template to a molecule, producing children (precursors). We'll need to decide which molecule each template applies to, ensuring that eventually we end with simple molecules (maybe commercially available). We don't need to verify buyability, just propose route.

We need to apply template 2895 to one of the precursors from previous step. Let's try applying to the larger fragment 'CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N1CCN(c2cc(N)cc3c2OC2(CCC2)CC3)CC1'. Use apply_template.
